facts.raw_span: A 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
presented with a 3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor
a 6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
extending craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale

concepts.why: The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with multiloculated cystic areas and hemorrhagic foci, along with smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex and clivus, is consistent with a chordoma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, along with smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex and clivus, is consistent with a chondrosarcoma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, along with dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles, is consistent with a meningioma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with multiloculated cystic areas and hemorrhagic foci, along with compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, is consistent with a hemangioblastoma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, along with smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex and clivus, is consistent with a schwannoma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with multiloculated cystic areas, along with smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex and clivus, is consistent with an epidermoid cyst.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with multiloculated cystic areas, along with smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex and clivus, is consistent with an arachnoid cyst.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, along with dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles, is consistent with a craniopharyngioma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, along with dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles, is consistent with a pituitary adenoma.

The presence of a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, along with dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles, is consistent with a glioma.
